# Phase 158 Reorg Work Measurements

Observed 2026-10-09 UTC (2026-10-08 CDT), lifecycle `158-2026-10-08T02-17-15`. Rust `1.94.1 (e408947bf 2026-03-25)`, Bun `1.3.9`. These are new Phase 158 observations; the historical Phase 157 report is unchanged.

## Actual experiment

```bash
PATH=/tmp/open-bitcoin-bun-1.3.9-fresh:$PATH bun run scripts/command-timings.ts run --key phase158-reorg-measure -- cargo test --manifest-path packages/Cargo.toml -p open-bitcoin-node --lib phase158_reorg_measurements -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The ignored experiment was explicitly executed: **one test passed, zero failed/ignored, 295.15s harness**. It completed **54 concrete Fjall configurations and 149 ordinary bounded turns**, with no peers, downloads, manual activation or retained stage. Raw output was captured in `/tmp/phase158-reorg-measurements.log`; all configuration observations and complete turn ledgers are preserved below so that temporary log is not the durable evidence owner.

Prefixes 16/128/512 have 32 successors. Fork depths are 1/8/32; replacements have the same depth or three additional blocks. Three seeded index positions per configuration yield actual post-startup progress before, within or after the fork where a nonempty interior exists. The configured startup's real eight-block turn is observed. “Seeded” counts records, while processed/safe entries are heights. The compact fixture deliberately uses coinbase maturity one; the separate unchanged maturity-100 fixture and subsequent ordinary validated connect remain Plan 05 evidence.

## What the counters and times mean

- Preparation returns immutable **storage preparation, native required-source preflight, captured genuine next-height facts, total** observations from the actual serialized manager preparation. The genuine stage and capabilities are dropped before returning. Each component fits its independently existing ceiling, and checked component addition equals the total. Production validates the composed ceiling before preview/commit.
- Preparation elapsed includes the preexisting consensus stage and index preparation together. Acceptance elapsed includes replacement-body saves, repeated genuine stage/preflight, preview/history work, mempool effects and guarded rewind publication. These are measured whole calls, **not isolated new-index timings** or a subtraction-derived delta.
- Actual BASIC point reads are counted around preparation and the complete production reorg call. Their difference observes the additional publication path, but does not invent a separate elapsed time or completed-rewind ledger readout. The rewind publisher independently admits its work against its existing cap before its guarded SyncAll batch; source review confirms one atomic state/owner/lock batch, without suffix deletion or a durable rewind cursor.
- Every turn's `TurnWork` includes acquisition, source admission, generation, authorization, preparation and completion. Turn authority hold includes storage; storage time is the complete append completion call, including validation and SyncAll, rather than isolated fsync latency. All 149 observed turns wrote one batch each.
- Work bytes/counts are conservative software reservations over actual selected data, not RSS, allocation-profiler results, comparison-profiler results, filesystem syscall counts or a wall-time guarantee. Preparation body bytes mix borrowed replacement representations and native required-source bytes. The first replacement turn borrows its captured fact; later turns read/decode their next actual bodies.

Fully indexed equal-depth representatives use the same new storage-preparation operations: **20 record / 8 projection / 3,221 checkpoint**, 5,096 reserved clone bytes and **16 actual BASIC point reads**. The complete production reorg uses **36 actual BASIC point reads** in these cases. Required sources scale with fork depth; native envelope byte lengths vary with encoded heights, independently of any full-prefix scan. The first full eight-record replacement turn in a fully indexed equal-depth-eight case used seven body reads/decodes/undo borrows and eight generations, 72 record operations, 42 projection operations and 44 BASIC point reads. A later full eight-body turn used 98 record operations and 56 point reads; projection work also reflects whether rows need incompatible-suffix replacement. These are current Phase 158 values, not historical Phase 157 numbers.

## Existing finite limits and refusal

No new numeric production cap was introduced. Measurements fit the independent existing storage, required-source and accepted-fact envelopes. The total preparation ceiling is the **checked sum** of those existing ceilings, not a new cap copied from an observed average. Existing normal turns retain eight blocks / 1 MiB body / 4 MiB undo / 16 MiB clones / 4 Mi item-work / 32 Mi byte-work / 1 MiB encoded / 512 record / 1,000,000 checkpoint / 256 projection operations. Absolute singleton policy remains one block / 128,000,000 body / 256 MiB undo / 1 GiB clones / 128 Mi item-work / 64 Gi byte-work / MAX_SIZE+170 encoded and the same operation ceilings.

Storage reorg work retains its existing singleton-sized clone/operation cap. Required-source preflight uses the existing absolute source/operation dimensions with normal block dimension. Fact capture retains 384 MiB byte/allocation dimensions and 1,000,000 item cap. The normal-suite checks individually validate all components plus their checked sum against these independently existing maxima; later publisher completion remains inside its own admitted storage envelope.

The normal suite checks exact measured record-acquisition admission (five operations accepted, four refused), absolute checkpoint-acquisition exhaustion before generated/published rows, inherited generation/revision exhaustion, and a fully retained but over-budget shared gap. In the last case a 401-block history indexed through actual startup height 23 forks at 390 with ten replacements. Existing source admission refuses `BASIC append work budget` before preview, accepted progress, mempool, checkpoint or lock changes. All required bodies/undo exist. Thus arbitrary retained-fork acceptance or unlimited lag is **not** claimed; this internal resource-policy limitation needs the Phase 07 parity documentation.

Existing core staging/preview clones and mempool/history processing remain dependent on their existing history and transition paths. The bounded new index counters do not establish whole-reorg constant work, constant memory, hard latency or public-mainnet/archive readiness. The automatic-prune evidence separately crosses the actual regtest threshold using 1,025 genuinely validated compact-history blocks and is not an inexpensive benchmark.
